subject.title: fix(zalo): add timeouts to Bot API requests

question: Should ordinary Zalo Bot API operations adopt a 30-second client-side deadline by default, accepting that slower successful responses will now abort?
rationale: The implementation and proof establish that a bounded deadline fixes the hang, but Zalo documents 30 seconds specifically for getUpdates rather than as a universal non-poll endpoint contract, so the exact default is an availability-policy choice.

options.title: Approve 30 seconds
options.body: Land the centralized default and retain explicit longer deadlines for long polling or any operation later shown to need one.

options.title: Choose another ceiling
options.body: Select an owner-approved ordinary-call timeout and update the implementation, tests, and controlled-server proof to match.

recommendation.title: Approve 30 seconds
recommendation.body: Land the centralized default and retain explicit longer deadlines for long polling or any operation later shown to need one.

likelyOwner.reason: The current client and its existing timeout policy originate in his commit, giving him the strongest evidence-backed ownership signal for the duration choice.
